# PART A — Examples of Conditional Statements

Example A: if ... else
```{r}
score <- 78

if (score >= 75) {
  print("Passed")
} else {
  print("Failed")
}
```

Example B: if ... else if ... else
```{r}
score <- 86

if (score >= 90) {
  print("Excellent")
} else if (score >= 80) {
  print("Good")
} else if (score >= 75) {
  print("Fair")
} else {
  print("Needs Improvement")
}
```

Example C: ifelse()
```{r}
scores <- c(92, 68, 75, 81, 59)

ifelse(scores >= 75, "Passed", "Failed")
```

Example D: Combining Conditions
```{r}
grade <- 91
attendance <- 95

if (grade >= 90 & attendance >= 90) {
  print("Honors candidate")
}
```

# PART B — Conditional Statements

Question 1
```{r}
temp <- 33

if (temp >= 32) {
  print("Hot")
} else {
  print("Not hot")
}
```

Question 2
```{r}
age <- 17

if (age < 13) {
  print("Child")
} else if (age <= 19) {
  print("Teenager")
} else {
  print("Adult")
}
```

Question 3
```{r}
marks <- c(45, 88, 73, 100, 62)

result <- ifelse(marks >= 60, "Pass", "Fail")

print(result)
```

Question 4
```{r}
x <- 10

if (x > 5) {
  print("A")
} else if (x > 8) {
  print("B")
} else {
  print("C")
}

# The output is A because x is greater than 5.
# R stops when the first TRUE condition is found.
```

Question 5
```{r}
# if is used for one condition at a time.
# ifelse() is used to check multiple values in a vector.
# Use if for single conditions and ifelse() for vectors.
```

```{r}
grades <- read.csv("students_grades.csv")
head(grades)
```

b. 
```{r}
if (file.exists("students_grades.csv")) {
```

```{r}
dim(grades)
```

f.1
```{r}
grades$FinalGrade <- round(
  grades$Quiz * 0.30 +
  grades$Midterm * 0.30 +
  grades$Final * 0.40,
  2
)

grades$FinalGrade
```

f.2 
```{r}
grades$Result <- ifelse(
  is.na(grades$FinalGrade),
  "Incomplete",
  ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 75, "Passed", "Failed")
)

grades$Result
```

f.3
```{r}
grades$Remarks <- ifelse(
  is.na(grades$FinalGrade), "Incomplete",
  ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 90, "Excellent",
  ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 85, "Very Good",
  ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 80, "Good",
  ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 75, "Fair", "Needs Improvement"))))
)

grades$Remarks
```

f.4 
```{r}
grades$AttendanceFlag <- ifelse(
  grades$Attendance < 80,
  "At Risk",
  "OK"
)

grades$AttendanceFlag
```

f.5 
```{r}
grades$Honors <- ifelse(
  !is.na(grades$FinalGrade) &
    grades$FinalGrade >= 90 &
    grades$Attendance >= 90,
  "Yes",
  "No"
)

grades$Honors
```

f.6 
```{r}
grades$LoopRemarks <- character(nrow(grades))

for (i in 1:nrow(grades)) {
  if (is.na(grades$FinalGrade[i])) {
    grades$LoopRemarks[i] <- "Incomplete"
  } else if (grades$FinalGrade[i] >= 90) {
    grades$LoopRemarks[i] <- "Excellent"
  } else if (grades$FinalGrade[i] >= 85) {
    grades$LoopRemarks[i] <- "Very Good"
  } else if (grades$FinalGrade[i] >= 80) {
    grades$LoopRemarks[i] <- "Good"
  } else if (grades$FinalGrade[i] >= 75) {
    grades$LoopRemarks[i] <- "Fair"
  } else {
    grades$LoopRemarks[i] <- "Needs Improvement"
  }
}

grades$LoopRemarks
```

f.7 
```{r}
# Run this line separately in the Console:
# if (grades$FinalGrade >= 75) print("Passed")

# R gives a warning because the condition has more than one value.
# A plain if statement expects one TRUE or FALSE value.
# A loop checks one student's grade at a time.
```


# Part D — Exporting Results to CSV

Question 7
a.
```{r}
write.csv(grades, "students_grades_processed.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

b.
```{r}
at_risk <- grades[grades$AttendanceFlag == "At Risk", ]

if (nrow(at_risk) > 0) {
  write.csv(at_risk, "at_risk_students.csv", row.names = FALSE)
  print("At-risk students exported.")
} else {
  print("There are no at-risk students.")
}
```

c.
```{r}
honors <- grades[
  grades$Honors == "Yes",
  c("StudentID", "Name", "Section", "FinalGrade", "Attendance")
]

if (nrow(honors) > 0) {
  write.csv(honors, "honors_list.csv", row.names = FALSE)
  print("Honors list exported.")
} else {
  print("There are no honors candidates.")
}
```

d.
```{r}
processed_check <- read.csv("students_grades_processed.csv")
at_risk_check <- read.csv("at_risk_students.csv")
honors_check <- read.csv("honors_list.csv")

head(processed_check)
head(at_risk_check)
head(honors_check)

dim(processed_check)
dim(at_risk_check)
dim(honors_check)
```

Question 8
```{r}
# 1. The missing Midterm value is saved as a blank field by default.
#    When the CSV is read back into R, it is recognized as NA.

# 2. Without row.names = FALSE, R adds an extra column containing
#    row numbers.
```

Question 9
a and b.
```{r}
grades$Scholarship <- ifelse(
  is.na(grades$FinalGrade), "Pending",
  ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 95 & grades$Attendance >= 90, "Full",
  ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 85 & grades$Attendance >= 90, "Partial", "None"))
)

grades$Scholarship
```

c.
```{r}
scholarship_candidates <- grades[
  grades$Scholarship %in% c("Full", "Partial"),
  c("StudentID", "Name", "Section", "FinalGrade", "Attendance", "Scholarship")
]

scholarship_candidates
```

d.
```{r}
if (nrow(scholarship_candidates) > 0) {
  write.csv(
    scholarship_candidates,
    "scholarship_candidates.csv",
    row.names = FALSE
  )
  print("Scholarship candidates exported.")
} else {
  print("There are no scholarship candidates.")
}
```

e.
```{r}
table(grades$Scholarship)
```

Question 10 
```{r}
# 1. is.na() is checked first because a missing grade cannot be
#    compared normally with a number.

# 2. If Failed is checked before Incomplete, a missing grade may
#    produce NA instead of the correct Incomplete label.

# 3. ifelse() is better for checking many values in a vector.
#    if ... else is better for one decision at a time.

# 4. Reading an exported CSV back into R helps check that the file
#    was saved correctly and contains the expected data.
```
